[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Full-Text Search and Spatial Indexes in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern database applications often require searching through vast amounts of textual data or querying geographic and geometric coordinates. MySQL provides native support for both Full-Text Search (FTS) and Spatial Data Types, backed by specialized indexes that make these operations performant."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Part 1: Full-Text Search in MySQL"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Full-text indexing allows you to perform complex natural language queries on string columns (CHAR, VARCHAR, or TEXT). Unlike standard LIKE queries, full-text search scores results based on relevance and handles stop-words automatically."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Full-Text Index"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE articles (
    id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    body TEXT,
    FULLTEXT KEY idx_title_body (title, body)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying with MATCH() ... AGAINST()"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To search within a full-text index, you must use the MATCH() function against the indexed columns, passing the search term to the AGAINST() function."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"SELECT id, title, MATCH(title, body) AGAINST('database optimization' IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE) AS relevance
FROM articles
MATCH(title, body) AGAINST('database optimization' IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE);
ORDER BY relevance DESC;"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Natural Language Mode: The default mode where the search string is treated as a phrase of human natural language."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Boolean Mode: Allows operators such as + (must be present), - (must not be present), and * (truncation operator)."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Part 2: Spatial Indexes in MySQL"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL supports spatial data types based on the OpenGIS geometry model, including POINT, LINESTRING, and POLYGON. Spatial indexes in InnoDB are implemented using R-Trees."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Spatial Table and Index"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE stores (
    id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100),
    location POINT NOT NULL,
    SPATIAL KEY idx_location (location)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Note that columns used in a spatial index must be declared as NOT NULL."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Inserting Spatial Data"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can insert geographic coordinates using the ST_GeomFromText or ST_PointFromText functions, specifying the longitude and latitude."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"INSERT INTO stores (name, location) VALUES 
('Downtown Branch', ST_GeomFromText('POINT(-73.985135 40.748817)', 4326)),
('Uptown Branch', ST_GeomFromText('POINT(-73.963244 40.779437)', 4326));"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying Spatial Data"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spatial functions like ST_Contains, ST_Intersects, and ST_Distance_Sphere allow you to calculate proximity and spatial relationships efficiently."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"SELECT name, ST_Distance_Sphere(location, ST_GeomFromText('POINT(-73.985000 40.748000)', 4326)) AS distance_meters
FROM stores
ORDER BY distance_meters ASC;
LIMIT 5;"},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"By leveraging MySQL Full-Text indexes and Spatial R-Tree indexes, developers can build high-performance search engines and location-aware applications directly within the relational database layer without needing external search servers."}]
